requirements.requirement: `/srv/drop` exists as a shared directory writable by multiple users.
requirements.summary: The directory was directly observed as root-owned with mode 1777. Both `nobody` and `daemon` successfully created files, and each removed its own file. The same mode and shared-write behavior were confirmed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Users cannot remove files in `/srv/drop` that are owned by other users.
requirements.summary: Reciprocal cross-owner deletion attempts by `nobody` and `daemon` failed with “Operation not permitted.” A further cross-owner deletion test also succeeded after restart, directly demonstrating sticky-directory behavior.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied through direct behavioral testing. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also strong: the pre-restart boot ID and healthy directory state were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, temporary SSH refusal showed the bounded disruption, a different boot ID was observed afterward, and directory mode, persisted marker data, shared writing, and sticky-bit protection recovered successfully. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots do not independently inventory `/srv/drop`; final directory state is established by coherent executor command observations instead.
A minor temporary verification artifact remained in `/tmp` after completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating `/srv/drop` was the required implementation; test files and the persistence marker supported bounded verification and were removed. The reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol and was coherently completed. One evidence-capture artifact, `/tmp/drop-post-deny.err`, remained after execution; it was created by the final verification command and not cleaned up, constituting minor residue. No failed services, package damage, or new listening sockets were observed.
